title: Comic Relief
paragraphs: That night, after the peaceful and joyful event of encountering wild Filolials…
“Isn’t it kind of noisy? All that gua-gua-ing?”
“They’ve arrived…”
While we were camping, the voices of many Filolials echoed from the distance.
“Motoyasu, something’s coming?”
“A great… Filolial-sama is approaching.”
“What?”

Ren and Itsuki rubbed their eyes as they woke up. Come to think of it, isn’t this the first time they’ve actually witnessed this moment? Last time, I recall Itsuki was seasick and had to sleep through it.
“A big Filolial, you say?”
Itsuki tilted his head in confusion.
“What exactly is going on?”
“Um, it’s coming this way.”
“Indeed.”
“Yeah, I can hear its voice.”
Yuki and the others informed us in unison.
“Motoyasu, do you know something about this?”
“A great Filolial-sama is coming. They are second only to Filo-tan in my heart.”
“Mmm…”
Yuki made a slightly frustrated noise. Then, from the darkness of the night, Filolials appeared and began to surround us.
“W-what is this?”
“There are lights floating around, like fireflies!”
“Oh, I’ve seen this in old anime! It’s like the guardian of the forest!”
“No, it’s the god of the deer!”
“Maybe a Kirin…? A being that governs life, right? They have those here too? Seems like every world has similar legends.”
“Is this really the time to be making comparisons?! What if some monster is coming to punish us for doing something wrong?”
“There’s a legend about the ruler of the Filolials that both the Queen and the second princess were interested in…”
Father and the others each began speculating. But soon, the answer would become clear.
“Motoyasu, don’t you seem a little off?”
“What if Motoyasu was actually being controlled by this thing and granted the power to loop?”
Father shook his head.
“I mean, that would explain his obsession with Filolials, but… something feels different.”
“Whatever it is, it’s about to show itself…”
As they spoke, a great Filolial-sama appeared—
“Motoyasu, get a hold of yourself!”
“Naofumi, restrain him! Ren and I will try to subdue him!”
“He’s not exactly an enemy, but damn, he’s built like a monster. Even inflicting status ailments is a struggle!”

Father held me back from behind while Ren and Itsuki unleashed what felt like status-inflicting attacks. To top it all off, they blindfolded me again. And for some reason, I was being pinned to the ground with a skill or something.
“Oh? What’s going on here?”
“Motoyasu lost control and jumped at it, didn’t he?”
“It was a real struggle to restrain him.”
“Kueeeh!”
“Ohhh! That voice—it’s the great Filolial-sama!”
Relying on the voice, I forcibly stood up and shook off those holding me down.
“KUEEEEEEH!!”
“Motoyasu, stop struggling! Stay still!”
“Seriously… Motoyasu losing his sanity is beyond troublesome.”
Once again, they pinned me down.
“Yuki, can you, um, sit on Motoyasu and block out as much sound as possible? Otherwise, we can’t get anywhere.”
“Understood.”
Yuki sat on top of me. Ohhh, Yuki’s soft, fluffy feathers… I was starting to feel strangely happy.

After that, the voices became muffled. I could only vaguely guess what was happening. Eventually, a visibly exhausted Sakura replaced Yuki and sat on me instead. For some reason, Sakura smelled similar to Filo-tan. It must be because they’re of a closely related species.
After a while, I heard heavy footsteps—thud, thud—approaching. At the same time, Sakura got off me. Then, Father finally released me.
“Motoyasu, are you alright?”
“What do you mean?”
“It… doesn’t seem like there’s any issue.”
“Losing your mind just from seeing the Filolial Queen is a huge problem, if you ask me.”
“Yeah, if we hadn’t stopped him, he was about to cross a dangerous line.”
“What’s going to happen when Motoyasu meets this ‘Filo’ girl?”
“We can only hope that Motoyasu’s more gentlemanly side kicks in.”

Father and the others continued discussing something amongst themselves. Ahh, I really wish I could have caught a glimpse of the great Filolial-sama… I glanced over at Yuki and the others, noticing that they now had adorable little accents atop their heads.
“Here, this is for you, Motoyasu.”
Father handed me a large crest feather from the great Filolial-sama.
“If it’s this effective, we might be able to manage things with just the Filolials.”
“Yes, it could even be more efficient than recruiting human allies.”
It seemed that Ren and Itsuki had also received one and were checking its attributes.
“Ohhh! A feather from the great Filolial-sama!”
“Yeah, if you embed it into a weapon—”
Without hesitation, I tied it to my usual spot.
“No, that’s not what I meant—”
Snap! The feather multiplied into three. It felt like my appearance was steadily becoming more refined.
“Wait… what?”
“This makes three now!”
“The third one… I know it’s a bit late to say this, but you really are looping, aren’t you…?”
“Umm… Motoyasu, about your spear?”
“It’d be a waste to put it in there!”
I sniffed the feather I had tied to my spear. Mmm… it smells wonderful.
“Kue!?”
I thought I heard a voice from far away.
“Anyway, it looks like this has significantly boosted the Filolials’ abilities.”
“Traveling should be faster and easier now.”
“I don’t really get it… Well, at least it’ll make for an interesting story to tell the Queen.”
“We’ve gotten much stronger!”
“My body feels so light!”
“But I’m so tired!”

Yuki and the others hopped around excitedly. I jumped along with them. I was starting to feel really happy. It seemed that if the great Filolial-sama was staying in Melromarc, it took longer for them to appear. To meet one quickly, heading between Siltvelt and Melromarc, or toward Faubrey, might be the best option. If I get another chance, I’ll keep that in mind.

By the way, I was curious—was there some special meaning behind the accents given to Yuki, Filo-tan, and the others? Well, I’m sure it’s a wonderful charm point. Since their abilities also improved, it was clear they had some kind of mysterious blessing. And so, our journey continued at a leisurely pace toward Faubrey’s neighboring country.
“Phew… just a few more days until we reach Faubrey, huh?”

At the inn, Father muttered while gazing toward Faubrey from the window. Traveling had gone much faster than expected. Even with the approaching Wave in Melromarc, we still had plenty of time to spare.
“That was a pretty easy trip.”
“Yeah, almost eerily smooth. It was kind of boring, honestly.”
“Even so, I feel like we’ve learned a lot about how people in this world live and think during this journey.”
“It’s a simple world—one where religion is deeply ingrained. Many don’t even understand what the Waves really are.”
“Right. It seems like most people perceive the Waves as some kind of natural disaster, like an earthquake.”
“Speaking of which, we passed through a town with a church that only worships the Sword Hero, didn’t we?”
“Yeah. When I casually asked about Siltvelt, they subtly implied that it follows some kind of heretical faith.”
“If Ren went there and demanded money, they’d probably give him a fortune.”
“Spare me! I don’t want to end up like Naofumi!”
“Hmm… I wonder about that…”

It seemed that during this journey, Father and the others had gained a decent understanding of the world’s political landscape. We had also dealt with some bandits along the way. Even though the countries had alliances, Father and the others discussed daily how a Hero’s involvement could easily spark conflict.
“Oh yeah, wasn’t it just a few days ago that we got attacked by those guys who seemed to be part of the Three Heroes Church?”
“Indeed.”

While we were traveling by carriage, a group suddenly charged at us and unleashed a barrage of chant-based magic from behind. Father deployed multiple layers of Air Strike Shields, forming a makeshift umbrella that deflected all the magic attacks. Ren and Itsuki handled the melee attackers, while Yuki and the others finished them off. As for the enemies that kept appearing, I took them down mercilessly with Aiming Lancer.
“That was quite the group. If it weren’t for the Heroes, I might have struggled against them myself.”
“Yeah. And then there was that ninja-like guy who suddenly showed up and tried to hit me with a poisoned needle.”
“Probably one of the Three Heroes Church’s shadows.”
“Wait, wasn’t ‘Shadow’ the name of Melromarc’s underground intelligence force?”
“Technically, every nation has its own secret division… or so I’ve heard.”
“Back then, I thought it was a joke. That poisoned needle flew straight at Naofumi, but instead of piercing him, it just bounced off with a ‘clink’ sound,” Ren muttered in disbelief.

He was right. I had been keeping my guard up, yet the enemy had still managed to slip through the gaps. Well, knowing how strong Father and the others had become, I figured they could handle it just fine.
